**Step 1 — Scene:** A vegetable-based meal of yellow seasoned rice, cooked green beans, and a leafy salad.

**Step 2 — Vessel:** A rounded-square dinner plate, approximately 26 cm across. Using a circular approximation: 3.14 × 13² ≈ **530 cm²**.

**Step 3 — Items:** Yellow rice with small vegetable pieces; green beans; spinach leaves; onion slivers; apparent avocado pieces; visible oil/dressing sheen.

**Steps 4–6 — Area, volume, and weight:**

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Density | Weight |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Yellow rice | 30% | 159 cm² × 2 cm = 318 ml | 0.8 | 254 g |
| Green beans | 22% | 117 cm² × 1.7 cm = 199 ml | 0.6 | 119 g |
| Spinach leaves | 23% | 122 cm² × 2.5 cm = 305 ml | 0.15 | 46 g |
| Apparent avocado | 3% | 16 cm² × 2 cm = 32 ml | 0.6 | 19 g |
| Onion | 2% | 11 cm² × 1 cm = 11 ml | 0.6 | 6 g |

Food coverage totals **80%**. Oil/dressing coats these foods rather than occupying additional plate area; estimate **8 g**.

**Step 7 — Energy:** Rice at 160 kcal/100 g contributes about 406 kcal; beans at 35 contribute 42 kcal; spinach at 23 contributes 11 kcal; avocado at 160 contributes 30 kcal; onion at 40 contributes 2 kcal; oil at 884 contributes 71 kcal. The rice estimate includes its cooking fat; the separate oil estimate is for the vegetables and salad.

**Step 8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **452 g and 562 kcal** is plausible for the visible rice mound, substantial bean portion, and loose salad. Rice depth and oil quantity are the main uncertainties.
